title: Unified queue discovery artifacts and bounded concurrency
summary: Create validated uncapped queue discovery artifacts in one backend traversal and let PowerShell curate transported metadata with a legacy-scan fallback.
reason: Remove the redundant Python inventory then PowerShell recursive rescan path while preserving deterministic queue policy and a fail-safe legacy scanner.
behavior_before: The backend produced a capped inventory and then PowerShell recursively enumerated and restatted the same sources before curation.
behavior_after: The backend writes complete checksum-bound JSONL candidate metadata under State/Progress/QueueScans, validates it, and passes its manifest through a backend-only pipeline argument. PowerShell validates it again and curates metadata records; uncertainty records a reason and invokes the legacy scanner.
tests_added: Python artifact checksum, scope, completeness, metadata, and curate-only reuse checks
manual_validation: Adversarial review covered corrupt checksum, out-of-scope paths, incomplete state, candidate-count mismatch, retention boundaries, and legacy fallback before queue execution.
24 targeted and adjacent Python queue/API tests passed; Ruff and targeted mypy passed.
PowerShell library-index and queue-engine checks passed; full active reliability regression suite passed.
Generated summary freshness passed for 2,332 source files.
rollback_plan: Revert this change. Removing QueueDiscoveryManifestPath restores the existing recursive scanner; the QueueScans directories are derived state and may be removed after confirming no live lease references them.
notes: Python impact: adds derived-artifact production/validation and bounded two-authority traversal. The public inventory remains preview-capped while execution candidates are written uncapped. No source, scratch, publish, FFmpeg, subtitle, or audio policy changes. Representative real-media validation remains required for PRs 4 and 5, not this discovery-only PR.
